extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, stakeholders and interested persons who want to find FEC rulemaking materials or participate in FEC rulemakings (e.g., submit comments or testify)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and resources for locating FEC rulemaking materials and participating in the Commission's rulemaking process (searching proposed/final rules, submitting public comments, and testifying at hearings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Search completed and ongoing Commission rulemakings. Search for proposed rules, final rules, public comments and hearing testimony. Additionally, submit comments on proposed regulations and other rulemaking documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the rulemakings search and advanced search (example: '2002-06') to find specific dockets; the search returns proposed rules, final rules, public comments and hearing testimony and provides means to submit comments on proposed regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search regulations (eCFR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current regulations are available on the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations, or eCFR, maintained by the National Archives. It is a continuously updated online version of the CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When needing the current text of Commission regulations, consult the eCFR (Electronic Code of Federal Regulations) for an up-to-date, continuously updated online source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed edition of 11 CFR
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the annual printed edition of 11 CFR. New regulations published after the 2025 printed edition will be included in the 2026 printed edition. Printed copies are available from the U.S. Government Bookstore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the annual printed editions of 11 CFR for an archival/printed reference; note that newly published regulations after the latest printed edition appear in subsequent printed editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanations and Justifications (E&Js)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission writes an E&J whenever it submits to Congress a new regulation or amends an old one. This archive compiles all E&Js written to accompany FEC regulations, from 1975 to present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Browse the E&J archive to find the Commission's explanatory statements accompanying regulations and amendments; E&Js provide the Commission's rationale and context for rule provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearings and testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission periodically holds public hearings at its headquarters in Washington, DC. These hearings offer interested persons an opportunity to testify concerning proposed regulations and other matters that come before the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the upcoming public hearings listing and the public hearings archive (listed in reverse chronological order with links to relevant documents) to learn about opportunities to testify or review prior testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand what triggers rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission initiatives, Congressional action, judicial decisions, or petitions for rulemaking may necessitate that the Commission update or adopt new regulations. Consequently, the FEC undertakes rulemakings either to write new Commission regulations or revise existing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that rulemakings arise from a variety of catalysts (internal initiatives, legislation, court decisions, petitions); understanding the trigger helps frame comments and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult primary legal authorities (caveat)
rubrics_metrics.description: This information is not intended to replace the law or to change its meaning, nor does this information create or confer any rights for or on any person or bind the Federal Election Commission or the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reader is encouraged to consult the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (52 U.S.C. 30101 et seq.), Commission regulations (Title 11 of the Code of Federal Regulations), Commission advisory opinions and applicable court decisions for authoritative legal guidance.
